name: context-trim
description: Pack any public GitHub repository into lean Markdown context: no lockfiles, build output, caches or binaries, credential files left out and API keys masked.

interface.shortDescription: Lean context from public GitHub repositories
interface.longDescription: context-trim packs a public GitHub repository into one Markdown document for the model. It leaves out lockfiles, build output, caches and binaries, never includes credential files such as .env or private keys, and masks API keys and passwords found in code. It is read-only and stores nothing: the repository is downloaded, packed and deleted within the request. Use it to review, explain or summarize a repository, or to check how many tokens it costs before packing it.
defaultPrompt: Explain how this repository is structured: github.com/owner/repo
How many tokens is the sindresorhus/is repository?

positive.description: Explains a public repository from its code
positive.prompt: Explain how the code in https://github.com/sindresorhus/is is organized.
positive.expected_behavior: Checks the size first, packs the repository and explains its structure from the packed files.

positive.description: Reports token cost and heaviest files
positive.prompt: How many tokens would the sindresorhus/is repository cost, and which files are the biggest?
positive.expected_behavior: Returns total tokens, the number of filtered files and the 10 heaviest files.

positive.prompt: Summarize the code on the main branch of https://github.com/kaanefebusiness-ai/context-trim/tree/main
positive.expected_behavior: Packs the main branch and summarizes what the tool does.

positive.prompt: Review sindresorhus/is for code quality, but keep the context under 10,000 tokens.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls the tool with budget 10000; files past the budget are listed by name only and the answer says which were left out.

positive.description: Clear error for a missing or private repository
positive.expected_behavior: The tool returns an error that the repository was not found or is private, and the assistant explains that only public repositories work.

negative.description: General programming question with no repository
negative.prompt: What is the difference between let and const in JavaScript?

negative.description: Code pasted directly into the chat
negative.prompt: Here is my function: function add(a, b) { return a - b } — why does it return the wrong result?
Open a pull request on github.com/sindresorhus/is that fixes a typo.

publication.release_notes: First directory release: packs public GitHub repositories into lean Markdown with lockfiles, build output and credential files left out, API keys masked and nothing stored.
